description: pyTCR is a Python model of rainfall caused by tropical cyclones. The JOSS paper describes a reduced-complexity physical method that follows storm tracks and accounts for moisture transport, wind shear and topographic forcing. Its own README links the code to cyclone-downscaling inputs and reports an MIT licence. Spatial coverage is the track and environmental grid supplied; temporal coverage is each storm or synthetic storm set. The rainfall fields can feed flood, drainage or compound-hazard simulations for exposed infrastructure. A caveat is that downscaled storms and simplified rainfall physics bring uncertainty, especially in rare-event tails and local topography. A rainfall estimate is not a flood-depth or asset-loss prediction without hydrological and hydraulic models. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own repository were read without downloading reanalysis data or simulating a cyclone.
name: pyTCR tropical-cyclone rainfall model
notes: G5 G5-0755. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
